description: The one active truth about what this product carries and how each of it is verified. It replaces build/test-infrastructure/capability-matrix.json, which classified only the source projects, and build/test-infrastructure/not-executed-inventory.json, which was a second list of the same categories kept by hand. Every project of this repository belongs to exactly one capability here, every required run names the job, the category and the project it starts, and every case that does not execute is named with its reason.

all.note: the complete required acceptance scope available to this work package: the local categories and the ones that run against a pinned fixture. It is defined here, so a narrower selection can never produce or satisfy an 'all' receipt.

fixture.note: everything that runs against the pinned Compose fixture

engineering.note: the retained engineering-model category; native diagnostics tests run in UnitArchitecture

verificationClasses.LOCAL_REQUIRED_RUN: A behaviour suite that runs in the required profile on the build machine alone. It needs no container and no credential.
verificationClasses.NATIVE_TEST_ESTATE: The inherited test project is retired after complete obligation closure. Product behavior is independently verified by the native xUnit/MTP estate under tests2 and .github/workflows/native-tests.yml; this model retains only product-project ownership and does not duplicate the native test contract.
verificationClasses.PINNED_FIXTURE_REQUIRED_RUN: A behaviour suite that runs in the required profile against a pinned container fixture from build/test-infrastructure/compose.yaml, started by tools/ci/run_broker_category.py.
verificationClasses.REAL_EPHEMERAL_CLOUD: A behaviour suite that needs a real, short lived cloud resource. It is not executed here and can never report a pass. This is a visible open proof, never a gate.
verificationClasses.COMPILE_AND_PACK_PROOF: A shipped capability with no behaviour suite of its own, exercised by the suites that use it. It is proven by compiling and packing.
verificationClasses.DEVELOPER_TOOL_COMPILE_PROOF: Not shipped to a consumer. It is proven by compiling, and by its own tests where it has them.
verificationClasses.SUPPORT_LIBRARY: Compiled and exercised through the capabilities that reference it; it carries no category of its own.

duenessClasses.NOT_DUE_EXTERNAL_INFRASTRUCTURE: Needs a service or credential this work package pins no fixture for. Forbidden in a category that runs against a pinned fixture: nine cases hid behind it while the broker they needed was exactly the one the required profile starts.
duenessClasses.NOT_DUE_BENCHMARK: Measures throughput or timing instead of behaviour.
duenessClasses.NOT_DUE_TIMING_SENSITIVE: Asserts against a wall clock interval and is not stable in a loaded full run.
duenessClasses.NOT_DUE_MANUAL_OBSERVATION: Produces output for a human; asserts nothing a gate could evaluate.
duenessClasses.NOT_DUE_ENVIRONMENT_DEPENDENT: Depends on host environment the run deliberately pins.
duenessClasses.NOT_DUE_DEFECTIVE_IMPORTED_ASSURANCE: Asserts an outcome its own configuration never engages. Measured against both engines, and kept out with the measurement written down until the intended mechanism is decided. The other five classes state why a sound case cannot run here; none of them can state that the case itself is unsound, and forcing it into one of them would be false.
duenessClasses.NOT_DUE_REAL_CLOUD_RESOURCE: Needs a real, short lived cloud resource that no container can stand in for. This is the only class a category with a pinned fixture may use, and it can never become a pass: the capability matrix carries the same statement as REAL_EPHEMERAL_CLOUD.

floorSemantics: minimumExecutedCases is the number of cases the category executed when it was last recorded. tools/ci/run_test_category.py fails a run that executes fewer, because coverage can fall without a single failure: a new exclusion, a renamed fixture or a narrowing filter all leave the counters green. Raising a floor is a normal part of adding cases; lowering one is a decision that belongs in a record.

openDefectsNotInventoried.statement: Empty. All five cases record 0025 raised as F-1 are closed by product corrections and by two adjustments the product owner authorised on 2026-08-10, which are to be reported to the lead architect. Every one of them now runs in the required category. A case leaves this list by being fixed and executed, never by being reclassified.

capabilities.rationale: The inherited Abstractions project is already retired. Its 70 executing and eight non-product or non-executing obligations are terminally bound in evidence/native-tests/abstractions/INHERITED_BEHAVIOR_DISPOSITION.json; the native Abstractions projects own the executable behavior contract.

All 115 inherited obligations are terminally bound in evidence/native-tests/analyzers/INHERITED_BEHAVIOR_DISPOSITION.json; the native Analyzer and CodeFix projects own the executable behavior contract.

The two deliberately started measurement scenarios gate nothing and are compile-proven by the Engineering solution. Their correctness contract now belongs to the native xUnit 4/MTP v2 Diagnostics project in the UnitArchitecture profile; the legacy category and its VSTest expected set are retired rather than taught to execute a second test architecture.

Five of the six Amazon S3 message-data obligations are owned by native xUnit 4/MTP v2 UnitArchitecture and LocalStack LocalIntegration tests. Real S3 lifecycle execution remains explicit External work and is not counted green.

Needs a real ephemeral cloud resource and is not verified here. It was linked to the transport capability of the same provider, which proved nothing: that capability has no run either, and sharing a test project is not sharing a proof.
The non-packable sample is compiled by the product and engineering solutions and carries no independent behavior category.

The inherited NUnit/VSTest project is retired after terminal closure of its OBL-R0-PER-0400 through OBL-R0-PER-0430 behavior inventory. Locally executable Azure Table behavior is verified by native xUnit 4/MTP v2 UnitArchitecture and Azurite LocalIntegration projects; OBL-R0-PER-0455 through OBL-R0-PER-0457 remain explicit External work and are not counted green.

The inherited NUnit/VSTest project is retired after terminal closure of all 10 DynamoDB obligations: eight are replaced by native xUnit 4/MTP v2 UnitArchitecture and LocalStack LocalIntegration tests, while two real-AWS service behaviors remain explicitly External and are not counted green.

The inherited NUnit/VSTest project is retired after terminal closure of all 90 assigned R0 obligations. EF Core behavior is verified by the native xUnit 4/MTP v2 UnitArchitecture and LocalIntegration projects.

The inherited NUnit/VSTest project is retired after complete closure of OBL-R0-PER-0200 through OBL-R0-PER-0286. Quartz behavior is verified by the native xUnit 4/MTP v2 project in the UnitArchitecture profile.

The inherited MessagePack serialization fixtures are retired after complete closure of OBL-R0-CORE-C-0153 through OBL-R0-CORE-C-0350 where applicable. MessagePack behavior and its hardened serializer-owner boundary execute in the native xUnit 4/MTP v2 project in the UnitArchitecture profile.
All 28 inherited obligations are terminally bound in evidence/native-tests/signalr/INHERITED_BEHAVIOR_DISPOSITION.json; the native SignalR project owns the executable behavior contract.

The native xUnit 4/MTP v2 visualizer project owns renderer and real state-machine graph-extraction contracts. The inherited visualizer obligations are terminally bound to those executing owners by the state-machine definition/runtime closure evidence; the native tests2 estate is intentionally outside this inherited verification model.

The run-scoped fixture contract every database backed test project reads. It carries no case of its own; it is compiled and exercised by the categories that reference it, and its own assurances are asserted in RunnerContract_Specs inside the SQL transport project.

The inherited NUnit/VSTest project is retired after terminal closure of all 113 ActiveMQ obligations and all 179 historical execution identities. Forty obligations are owned by the native UnitArchitecture project and seventy-three by the native LocalIntegration project, which executes against run-scoped ActiveMQ Classic and Artemis fixtures through the canonical broker runner. The terminal projection is .testagent/activemq-native-obligation-map.tsv; the native xUnit 4/MTP v2 estate is the sole executable behavior contract.

The inherited NUnit/VSTest project is retired after terminal closure of all 70 SQS obligations: 66 are replaced by executing native xUnit 4/MTP v2 tests, two remain explicit real-AWS External work, one raw-secret API obligation is superseded by the PO-approved SDK credential model, and one inherited scheduler case is a byte-semantic duplicate. The native UnitArchitecture and LocalIntegration projects own the executable behavior contract.

notExecuted.reason: Addresses a real Amazon MQ broker over TLS with an account nobody in this run has. The pinned RabbitMQ fixture cannot stand in for it, so it stays a visible open cloud proof and never a pass.

capabilities.rationale: The 135 frozen SQL obligations are terminal in the native xUnit/MTP estate: 134 execute across the hermetic, PostgreSQL and SQL Server owners, and the obsolete cross-provider runtime dialect resolver is explicitly retired.

notes.verifiedThroughCapability: A capability whose cases live in another capability's test project names that capability instead of claiming the project a second time. Every project belongs to exactly one owner, and a reader can still find where a capability is exercised.
notes.testAnchors: A capability verified through another one names the exact test fixtures inside that capability's test project which exercise it, each with the category whose run executes them. A namespace is not an anchor: it names every case that happens to live under it. A prose link is not a proof either - before a run the fixture is checked to be a declared class of that category's test project in a file that carries a test attribute, and during the run the category has to have executed at least one case whose fixture equals the anchor.
notes.selections: A selection is a named scope tools/ci/verify.py can be asked to verify. Its members are categories or other selections, and 'all' is defined here so that a narrower selection can never produce or satisfy an 'all' receipt.
notes.expectedIdentities: The exact identities a category is expected to execute, generated from a clean run of that category by tools/ci/verify.py --record-expected and never edited by hand. null means no complete clean run has recorded one yet, and a category in that state cannot be part of a passing receipt.
notes.budgetSeconds: How long a category's child process may take before its whole tree is taken down and the run is red. It is here rather than in a workflow because the canonical runner is also the local one, and a job timeout does nothing on a developer machine.
